analysis:
## Overall Health Assessment

The repository shows concerning stagnation with 70% of open issues being stale (30+ days without updates), indicating critical maintenance debt. While showstopper issues are under control, the aging backlog of 48 stale issues and inconsistent issue assignment patterns suggest resource constraints rather than active development.

## Top 3 Risks Requiring Immediate Attention

1. **70% stale rate** - 34 of 48 open issues have been untouched for 30+ days, risking knowledge loss and increasing technical debt
2. **Single-point-of-failure contributors** - sathyajith-pucar alone owns 20% of all open issues (14/69), creating a critical bottleneck
3. **48 issues with no contributor assigned** (11%) + unclear ownership patterns compromising accountability

## Actionable Recommendations

• **Implement automated stale issue triage**: Archive/assign owners to all 34 stale issues (>30 days) within 2 weeks or mark for closure
• **Redistribute workload**: Reassign 5+ issues from sathyajith-pucar to other team members (Hemadri-Chinna, anshumanth, ashishbeehyv) who already have 5+ issues
• **Enforce assignment policy**: Require every new issue to have an assignee within 48 hours of creation - automate reminder workflows
• **Prioritize oldest non-showstoppers**: Start with #4795 (367 days), #4823 (359 days), #4932 (335 days) - these represent highest risk legacy debt
• **Create rotation schedule**: Establish weekly backup owner assignments for long-running issues to prevent single-person bottlenecks

## Positive Signals

• **No showstopper issues** remaining - indicates stable core functionality
• **Active recent contributions** - 30 newest issues show ongoing development activity
• **Clean commit history** - absence of abandoned branches suggests disciplined workflow maintenance
